signalling.text: The D2 receptor couples to Gi/o proteins, inhibiting adenylyl cyclase and reducing neuronal excitability and dopamine release at terminals.

claim.text: D2 receptors are densely expressed in the dorsal and ventral striatum, where antipsychotic blockade produces both therapeutic response and extrapyramidal or prolactin effects.

signalling.text: The 5-HT2A receptor couples to Gq/11, activating phospholipase C and increasing cortical pyramidal excitability.

claim.text: 5-HT2A receptors are richly expressed across prefrontal cortex, where second-generation antipsychotics block them alongside D2.

signalling.text: The M1 receptor couples to Gq/11 and is concentrated postsynaptically in cortex and hippocampus, supporting memory and cognition.

claim.text: M1 receptors predominate in cortex and hippocampus; selective M1 activation is pursued for cognitive symptoms with fewer peripheral effects.

signalling.text: The M4 receptor couples to Gi/o and acts largely as an inhibitory autoreceptor and striatal modulator of dopamine release.

claim.text: M4 receptors in the striatum restrain dopamine release, which is the rationale for M4-preferring agonism in psychosis.

signalling.text: GluN2A is a regulatory subunit of the NMDA glutamate receptor, a calcium-permeable coincidence detector central to synaptic plasticity.

claim.text: GluN2A-containing NMDA receptors are prominent in hippocampus and cortex, including on parvalbumin interneurons implicated in the glutamate model of psychosis.
